scope_note: Triton AMD backend is no longer in-tree: flash_attn_interface.py imports aiter.ops.triton._triton_kernels.flash_attn_triton_amd from the third_party/aiter submodule (not initialised, not covered). hopper/ and flash_attn/cute contain no @triton.jit. 12 jit functions in k_activations.py and 2 in flash_attn_triton.py (_bwd_store_dk_dv, _bwd_kernel_one_col_block) are helpers.

families.reference: o = F.scaled_dot_product_attention(q.transpose(1,2), k.transpose(1,2), v.transpose(1,2), attn_mask=bias_bcast(+ top-left causal -inf mask torch.ones(Sq,Sk).tril().logical_not() if causal and bias given), is_causal=(causal and bias is None), scale=softmax_scale or 1/sqrt(d)).transpose(1,2); lse = torch.logsumexp(scale*q@k^T + bias + causal_mask, -1); backward = autograd grads of o w.r.t. q,k,v (no bias grad)
spec_sources: tests/test_flash_attn.py (triton race-condition tests referenced in docstring)
families.notes: Layout (B,S,H,D); fp16/bf16 only; d<=128; no GQA, no dropout, no varlen. Bias shape (B|1,H|1,1|Sq,Sk) in q dtype or fp32 ('vector' vs 'matrix'), added after scaling. Causal mask is TOP-LEFT aligned (offs_m >= offs_n), matching SDPA is_causal (unlike FA2 CUDA bottom-right). LSE stored in (B,H,ceil(Sq/128)*128) fp32 buffer. bwd: autotune may pick SEQUENCE_PARALLEL=True -> dq via tl.atomic_add (non-deterministic order); docstring warns of possible compiler race conditions for untested headdims. Uses removed Triton API tl.dot(..., trans_b=True) -> needs triton 2.0-era compiler or patch; hardware-wise plain (sm80-tested, fine on sm86).

families.family: flash_attn_triton_og (Triton tutorial fused attention, causal only)
families.reference: F.scaled_dot_product_attention(q, k, v, is_causal=True, scale=sm_scale); backward = autograd grads w.r.t. q,k,v
families.notes: Benchmark-only copy. Layout (B,H,N,D); always causal; no masking so N_CTX must be a multiple of 128; D in {16,32,64,128}; K/V offsets computed with Q strides (q,k,v must share layout/strides); fwd stores l and m separately; bwd pre-divides dO by l. Uses removed tl.dot trans_a/trans_b API.

families.family: cross_entropy (label smoothing, logit scale, z-loss, TP split)
families.reference: z = logit_scale*logits.double(); lse = torch.logsumexp(z,-1); loss = F.cross_entropy(z, labels, reduction='none', label_smoothing=smoothing, ignore_index=ignore_index) + torch.where(labels!=ignore_index, lse_square_scale*lse**2, 0); z_loss = torch.where(labels!=ignore_index, lse_square_scale*lse**2, 0); backward = autograd of loss w.r.t. logits (z_loss gets no grad)
families.notes: logits (rows, vocab) any float dtype, computed in fp32; per-row losses (reduction='none'). Smoothing convention = torch's (s*sum/C over total_classes). Deviation: non-ignored labels outside [0,n_cols) drop the CE term (loss = smoothing*(lse - mean logit) + z-loss) instead of raising like torch. PRECOMPUTED_LSE path only when smoothing==0 and logit_scale==1. SPLIT (process_group) path: kernel computes per-shard partial loss without LSE; final loss assembled in torch after all-reduce -> reference is the full-vocab loss, needs multi-rank emulation. inplace_backward overwrites logits.

families.reference: flash_attn.layers.rotary.apply_rotary_emb_torch: ro=2*cos.shape[-1]; c=repeat(cos[pos],'s d->s 1 (2 d)') (interleaved: '(d 2)'); out = cat([x[...,:ro]*c + rotate_half(x[...,:ro], interleaved)*s, x[...,ro:]], -1) with pos = arange(seqlen)+seqlen_offsets[b]; conjugate=True uses -sin (this is the backward)
families.notes: x (B,S,H,D) or varlen (total,H,D)+cu_seqlens (positions restart at 0 per sequence, plus seqlen_offsets int or (B,) tensor). cos/sin (seqlen_ro, rotary_dim/2) supplied by caller; rotary_dim<=headdim<=256, dims beyond rotary_dim copied through. Interleaved=GPT-J pairs, else NeoX halves. Computes in fp32. Positions >= seqlen_ro masked to cos=1,sin=0 (identity) rather than error (only asserted for int offsets). Backward is the same kernel with conjugate=True. Needs triton>=3.0 (tl.split/tl.join).

families.family: fused linear + activation (fwd) and activation-grad dgrad (bwd)
families.reference: fwd: pre = F.linear(x, weight, bias); out = act(pre) with act in {id, F.gelu(pre), F.gelu(pre, approximate='tanh'), F.relu(pre)**2}; act_input = pre if save_act_input. bwd (triton_dgrad_act): grad_input = (grad_output @ weight) * act'(act_input), i.e. autograd of the fwd w.r.t. x
families.notes: Same dtype for x/weight/bias; fp32 accumulate. Bug/deviation: kernel_fwd stores C without mask (mask computed but unused) -> out-of-bounds writes when M or N not divisible by BLOCK_M/BLOCK_N (reads are wrapped via rm%M). gelu uses tl.libdevice.erf and module imports triton.ops.matmul_perf_model -> both removed in modern Triton (3.x); needs old Triton. squared_relu_grad uses 2x for x>=0. Only 'id','gelu','gelu_approx','squared_relu' accepted by wrappers.

families.reference: layer_norm_ref / rms_norm_ref in the same file with dropout_p=0: h = x*rowscale[:,None] (+ x1) (+ residual); w' = w+1 if zero_centered_weight; y = F.layer_norm(h, (N,), w', b, eps) | F.rms_norm(h, (N,), w', eps) (+ b); y1 likewise with weight1/bias1; residual_out = h; backward = autograd (dw/db partials summed over programs)
families.notes: Rows of a 2D view, N*elem_size < 64KB; stats in fp32; mean/rstd saved. RMSNorm optionally has a bias added after scaling. residual_out may be stored in a different (e.g. fp32) dtype; x1 and rowscale mutually exclusive. bwd can RECOMPUTE_OUTPUT y; dw/db written as per-program partials then summed in torch.

families.reference: layer_norm_ref / rms_norm_ref(..., dropout_p=p, dropout_mask=mask, dropout_mask1=mask1) using the kernel's returned keep masks
open_decisions: RNG stream is tl.rand(seed_row, col, n_rounds=7) Philox with per-row int64 seeds from torch.randint; not bit-reproducible by torch
families.notes: Deterministic checks: with return_dropout_mask=True compare to the ref using the stored masks (inverted-dropout scaling 1/(1-p)); keep-rate ~ 1-p statistically; backward regenerates the same masks from the saved seeds -> check dx against autograd with the stored masks; p=0 reduces to the deterministic family.
